input.quote: 8.1 This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for three years unless earlier terminated in accordance with its terms.
input.rationale: Section 9 grants only for-cause rights: material breach (9.1), insolvency (9.2) and Customer's Vendor-default triggers (9.3), with 9.5 addressing cross-Order Form effect; 27.3 is a force-majeure exit and 6.2/19.4/20.5 are remedy-specific. No convenience termination right exists anywhere for Customer despite a three-year term, which is walk-away territory under T4C, so the fallback is not met either. Vendor likewise has no convenience right today, but silence gives us nothing to quote, so the inserted clause states it expressly; Section 8.2's 180-day non-renewal mechanic is a renewal term and is not flagged here. Inserted Section 9.4 in the existing numbering gap carries the preferred elements: 30 days' notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, and no Vendor convenience right during a committed term.

proposal.summary: Insert Section 9.4 giving Customer a 30-day convenience termination right with pro-rata refund and confirming Vendor has none during a committed term.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The three-year term gives us no way out absent Vendor default, so we have added our standard convenience right: termination of the Agreement or an Order Form on thirty days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, and confirmation that Vendor has no matching right during a committed term. If helpful, we can move to 60-90 days' notice with an early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees.

ops.text: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees pro rata for the period after the effective date of termination. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a committed term.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
